Video.title: Video
Video.description: Represents a video entry in the portfolio's video gallery, showcasing creative work or presentations.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Video entity.

title.description: The title of the video, displayed prominently in the gallery.

description.description: A brief description or summary of the video content, providing context to viewers.

videoUrl.description: The URL where the video is hosted (e.g., YouTube, Vimeo, or a direct link to the video file).

thumbnailUrl.description: The URL for the video's thumbnail image, used for previewing the video in the gallery.

durationInSeconds.description: The duration of the video in seconds.

isFeatured.description: A boolean flag indicating if this video should be prominently featured on the landing page. Only one video should be marked as featured at a time.

order.description: An optional numeric value to define the display order of the video within its gallery or list.

tagIds.description: References to Tags. (Relationship: Tag N:N Video)

createdAt.description: The date and time when the video record was created.

updatedAt.description: The date and time when the video record was last updated.

Tag.title: Tag
Tag.description: Represents a categorization tag used for filtering projects, videos, or other content within the portfolio.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Tag entity.

name.description: The name of the tag (e.g., 'React', 'Design', 'Animation', 'Web Development').

description.description: A brief description of what this tag represents, providing clarity on its use.

definition.description: Stores all video entries for the portfolio's video gallery. Each document is publicly readable and can be filtered by the 'isFeatured' flag to distinguish between landing page content and the full gallery. Write access is restricted to the administrator. Includes the 'isFeatured' field for presentation logic, and 'tagIds' for categorization.

params.name: videoId
params.description: Unique identifier for a specific video.

definition.description: Stores categorization tags used across the portfolio, such as for filtering videos or other content. Each document is publicly readable. Write access is restricted to the administrator.

params.name: tagId
params.description: Unique identifier for a specific tag.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure is designed to support a minimalist, modern portfolio site with a video gallery, prioritizing security, scalability, and debuggability. All videos and tags are stored in top-level collections, `/videos` and `/tags`, respectively. This approach simplifies access control and querying for a single-owner portfolio. Authorization Independence is achieved because all documents are self-contained for read access, eliminating the need for `get()` calls in security rules. Public read access to all videos and tags is granted, while write access is restricted to an administrator (the portfolio owner) via a global role check (e.g., against an `/admin_uids/{uid}` collection, though this specific collection isn't part of the data model entities, it's a common security pattern). This ensures that rules are simple and atomic.

Regarding Query Ability and Predictability (QAPs), the structure supports efficient querying:
1.  **Landing Page Video:** The `isFeatured` boolean flag in the `Video` document allows for a direct query to retrieve the single featured video for the landing page (`/videos.where('isFeatured', '==', true).limit(1)`). This is a highly efficient and predictable query, directly addressing the requirement without filtering on the client side or needing complex rule logic.
2.  **Video Gallery:** The remaining videos for the full gallery view can be retrieved by querying for `isFeatured == false` (`/videos.where('isFeatured', '==', false).orderBy('order')`) or simply retrieving all videos and filtering for non-featured ones on the client, depending on specific display logic. Using `orderBy('order')` ensures a predictable display sequence. The `tagIds` array in the `Video` document also allows for client-side filtering by tags, or potential `array-contains` queries if more advanced server-side filtering is required in the future.

Structural Segregation is maintained as all documents within `/videos` share the same security posture (public read, admin write). The `isFeatured` flag is a data attribute for content presentation, not an access control attribute, thus not requiring separate collections. The `Tag` collection follows the same principle, serving as a global lookup for categorization.
